//: The web client is one workspace in a monorepo, and it cannot be built on its own: @qmail/crypto has to be compiled and its WASM vendored first, then @qmail/core. Vercel therefore installs and builds from the repo root rather than from apps/web.
//rewrites: A single-page app: anything that is not a real file is the app itself.

headers.//: Nothing loads from anywhere but this origin, except calls to Supabase. 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is required and sufficient for the liboqs modules — they are instantiated from bytes already embedded in the bundle, so no separate .wasm is ever fetched. blob: covers decrypted attachments, which are built in memory and never served by anyone.
headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co wss://*.supabase.co; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

headers.//: The whole design rests on ciphertext never being readable by the server. It should not be readable by a downgrade attack either.
No feature here needs a camera, a microphone or a location, and a mail client asking for them would be a red flag.
Hashed asset filenames are immutable by construction.
The entry document must never be cached, or a deploy leaves people on a stale bundle pointing at assets that no longer exist.
